titleEn: Don't Know It? Don't Eat It—Ask First!

pages.text: "Grandma, there's something shiny here!" Yuki picked a bean-sized berry from a bush. They had come to the mountain path behind the house for raspberries. Grandma followed with a basket, brown dog Momo beside her.
"I'll fill the basket with raspberries today!" Yuki led the way. The round, shiny berry on their palm looked like a raspberry.
"This looks tasty, too!" Yuki lifted it toward their mouth. Grandma called from behind, "Wait!"
Grandma strode up and examined the palm. "You mustn't eat that. It will hurt your tummy." Startled, Yuki opened their hand. "I thought it was a raspberry..."
Grandma lightly touched Yuki's mouth. "Your mouth is our room's door. Only familiar things pass through." Yuki imagined the room's paper door.
"What if something unknown waits outside?" Grandma asked. Yuki put the berry back beneath the bush. "Don't Know It? Don't Eat It—Ask First!" came the firm answer.

Later, Yuki saw a bumpy mushroom under a tree. Before, Yuki might have popped it into their mouth, but now their lips stayed shut. "Don't Know It? Don't Eat It—Ask First!" Yuki hid both hands behind their back.
Yuki pointed to it. Grandma looked and shook her head. "Not that one either. Asking without touching was the right thing." Yuki's shoulders rose proudly.
Grandma held up three fingers. "One, don't touch! Two, leave it there and point! Three, ask a grown-up!" Yuki fixed the scarf knot. This time, familiar berries filled the basket.
Walking home, Grandma held Yuki's hand, swinging it gently. Eating only familiar things kept the tummy from hurting. "I know raspberries, so yum-yum! Don't Know It? Don't Eat It—Ask First!"
